title: What Is Waggle OS?
description: Start with the README to understand the product: a workspace-native AI agent platform whose distinguishing feature is persistent memory. This document lays out the architecture, the quick-start setup, and the environment variables, giving you the mental model of a memory-first AI workspace before you read a single line of code. Keep its 'memory is the moat' framing in mind — it explains why so much of the codebase orbits the substrate you will reach in Step 7.

title: Frontend Entry Point
description: This is where the running product actually begins. main.tsx is the React entry point that applies the stored theme before first paint (to avoid a flash of unstyled content), initializes analytics, and mounts the root App component, which in turn composes the full provider hierarchy: theme, Clerk auth, services, and install state, wrapped around the router. Following the import graph forward from here is the natural reading order for the entire UI.
languageLesson: React apps bootstrap by calling createRoot(...).render(<App/>). The provider 'hierarchy' in App.tsx is the idiomatic way to make cross-cutting concerns (auth, theme, data clients) available to the whole tree via Context, instead of threading props down manually.

title: The Desktop Cockpit Shell
description: One level deeper from App lies the AppShell — the top-level 'OS' surface that orchestrates the boot sequence, workspace state, keyboard shortcuts, the dock, overlay visibility, and the layout of Sidebar, StatusBar, and ChatHost. This is the component that makes Waggle feel like a desktop operating system rather than a web page. Everything the user interacts with hangs off this shell, so it is the hub of the frontend dependency graph (high fan-out).

title: How the UI Talks to the Backend
description: The frontend never calls the server directly — every request flows through the LocalAdapter, the single most depended-upon file in the UI (highest fan-in in the whole frontend). It wraps each sidecar API call, manages the connection lifecycle with session-token refresh and 401-retry, and exposes SSE subscriptions, all behind one shared singleton. The ServiceProvider wires that adapter into React context so any component can read connection state. Understanding this boundary is the key to understanding how the cockpit from Step 3 stays in sync with the server you meet next.
languageLesson: A singleton adapter behind a Context provider is a common pattern for centralizing all network I/O: retries, auth refresh, and streaming (SSE) live in one place, so call sites stay declarative and the cross-cutting connection logic is never duplicated.

title: The Server: Fastify Sidecar
description: On the other side of the adapter is the local sidecar — a Fastify server factory that registers roughly 80 route plugins and decorates the server with memory, vault, connectors, and scheduling infrastructure, seeding initial data on first run. This file is the backend's nerve center: it has the highest fan-out of any node in the project, because nearly every feature plugs a route into it. The adapter from Step 4 is calling exactly these routes.

title: The Chat Pipeline — Where It All Connects
description: Of the sidecar's many routes, the chat route is the spine of the product. It implements the full agent conversation pipeline: assembling the system prompt, scanning input for prompt injection, streaming the LLM response, executing tool calls, integrating memory, and delivering everything back over SSE. This single route ties together the agent runtime (Step 6's neighbor) and the memory substrate (Step 7), so it is the best vantage point for seeing how a user message becomes an agent action with memory recall.

title: Agent Runtime: Loop, Orchestrator, Personas
description: When the chat route runs an agent, it drives this subsystem. The agent-loop executes multi-turn LLM interactions, dispatching tool calls with retry logic, a loop guard, and completion gates. The orchestrator owns the memory substrate and builds each system prompt with persona and recalled-memory context, while the 17 built-in personas (pure data in persona-data, logic in personas) shape how each agent behaves. Together they turn the raw LLM into a memory-aware, role-specialized worker.
languageLesson: Splitting personas into a pure-data module (persona-data.ts) and a logic module (personas.ts) is a deliberate separation of concerns: the declarative array is easy to extend and test, while behavior (lookup, prompt composition, custom-persona loading) stays isolated and side-effect-aware.

title: Agent Tools — The Bridge to Memory
description: Agents act through tools, and the mind-tool factory is where the runtime meets the moat. It creates save_memory, search_memory, list_memories, get_entity, add_awareness, and feedback tools, each wired directly to the memory substrate (HybridSearch, KnowledgeGraph, IdentityLayer, the Cognify pipeline). This is the concrete handoff from 'agent' to 'memory': when an agent remembers or recalls, it is calling these tools, which is why this file ranks near the top of fan-in across the whole codebase.

title: The Memory Substrate — The Moat
description: This is the heart of Waggle's strategy: persistent memory that is free forever to create lock-in. db.ts opens the SQLite database and applies migrations; FrameStore implements video-codec-inspired I/P/B-frame memory compression with FTS indexing and dedup; HybridSearch fuses FTS5 keyword search, ANN vector search, RRF, and optional cross-encoder reranking; the KnowledgeGraph stores entity-relations with temporal validity; and the IdentityLayer persists who the user is. The tools from Step 8 are thin wrappers over exactly these classes.

title: Filling the Substrate: Harvest Ingestion
description: Memory does not only accumulate from live chats — the harvest pipeline imports existing conversations and files (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini exports, PDFs, URLs) into the substrate you just toured. It runs a classify → extract → synthesize flow with batched LLM calls, concurrency control, injection scanning, and deduplication, producing the memory frames that FrameStore (Step 9) stores. This is how a brand-new install becomes immediately useful: it harvests a user's history into the moat.

title: The Shared Data Model & Database Schema
description: Beneath both UI and server sits a shared vocabulary. The shared types module declares 30+ canonical interfaces (User, Team, AgentDef, Task, WaggleMessage, Memory, Artifact, Connector) used across every package, and tiers.ts encodes the 5-tier subscription system (TRIAL/FREE/PRO/TEAMS/ENTERPRISE) that gates features everywhere. The Drizzle schema and the generated SQL migration turn those types into the actual relational tables — agents, tasks, and team_entities (note the temporal validity windows that mirror the KnowledgeGraph from Step 9).
languageLesson: Drizzle ORM defines tables as TypeScript objects and generates SQL migrations from them, so the database schema and the application's types stay in lockstep — a single source of truth instead of hand-maintained SQL drifting from the code.

title: Supporting Systems & How It Ships
description: Finally, the systems around the core and how it reaches users. Evolution (EvolutionOrchestrator + IterativeGEPA) is a self-improvement loop that mutates and re-scores prompts behind quality gates; WaggleDance dispatches messages between agents for multi-agent coordination. To ship, the Tauri Rust shell registers IPC commands and the system tray, the Node sidecar runs as a bundled child process speaking over IPC, the three-stage Dockerfile produces a minimal Alpine image for the Teams server, docker-compose wires the local infra (Postgres, Redis, MinIO, LiteLLM), and the CI pipeline gates every push with type-checks, lint, unit, and E2E tests.
languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds (builder → native-builder → runtime) compile everything in fat intermediate stages but copy only the runtime artifacts into the final image, keeping the production image small while still rebuilding native modules like better-sqlite3 against the runtime's libc.
